subject.title: Preserve structured ACP backend error kinds instead of mapping all errors to `end_turn`

question: Should non-refusal Gateway chat failures in the ACP bridge reject `session/prompt` with `RequestError`, or keep resolving `PromptResponse` while exposing structured failure data through another approved surface?
rationale: The Gateway already has structured error kinds, but the ACP SDK stop-reason contract cannot represent several of them directly, and switching resolved prompts into JSON-RPC rejections is a client-visible compatibility choice.

options.title: Approve RequestError settlement after fixes
options.body: Use rejected `session/prompt` responses for backend failures, but require non-conflicting codes/data, intentional reconnect behavior, focused contract tests, and real ACP proof before merge.

options.title: Preserve resolved prompt responses
options.body: Keep the existing resolved `PromptResponse` model by default and expose structured failure information through an explicitly approved metadata or diagnostic surface.

options.title: Pause for replacement
options.body: Leave this issue open for a maintainer-led or refreshed implementation if the current branch cannot settle the compatibility contract and proof gap.

recommendation.title: Approve RequestError settlement after fixes
recommendation.body: Use rejected `session/prompt` responses for backend failures, but require non-conflicting codes/data, intentional reconnect behavior, focused contract tests, and real ACP proof before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: The structured error-kind implementation and focused ACP tests trace through recent area history to this owner signal.
